title: Consistent-hash shard router for orders and inventory
name: Order shard router

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code maps keys to shards? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A new shard node is added to a ring with 5 nodes and 128 virtual nodes each. Roughly what happens to key ownership?
choices: Nearly all keys are reassigned, since the modulus changes
About half of the keys move between existing nodes
Only about a sixth of keys move, and they all move to the new node
No keys move until remove_node is called for an old node

questions.prompt: Inside replicas(), why is the std::set of seen node names needed?
choices: Because consecutive ring points often belong to the same physical node via virtual nodes, so without it the same node could be returned several times
To keep the result sorted by node name
To avoid taking the shared lock twice
Because std::map iterators are invalidated when a node is added

questions.prompt: The loop in replicas() is bounded by `steps < ring_.size()`. What does that bound guarantee?
choices: The function skips virtual nodes that belong to removed shards
The walk starts at the first point of the ring rather than at the key's position
The walk visits each ring point at most once, so with fewer than `count` distinct nodes it returns all of them instead of looping forever
